options: A resource the business controls that provides future benefit
A present obligation of the business, from a past transaction, that will require a future outflow to settle
Any amount of cash sitting in the business's bank account
An asset that has lost all of its value
questions.explain: A liability is a present obligation arising from a past transaction, requiring a future outflow of economic benefit to settle.

questions.q: What is the most common liability on most companies' books, according to this lesson?
options: Bonds payable
Long-term notes payable
Mortgages payable
Accounts Payable — amounts owed to suppliers for goods or services already received
questions.explain: Accounts Payable, not loans, is the most common liability for most businesses — it arises simply from buying on credit.

questions.q: Caldwell Precision Works has a 10-year mortgage, with one month's payment due next month and the rest due over the following 9+ years. How is this classified?
options: The portion due within the next year is current; the remainder is long-term
The entire mortgage is a current liability
The entire mortgage is a long-term liability
Mortgages are never classified as liabilities
questions.explain: A single loan can straddle both categories: the part due within a year is current, and the rest is long-term.

questions.q: If Caldwell Precision Works buys $8,000 of raw materials on 30-day credit terms, what happens?
options: Nothing is recorded until the invoice is paid
It records an $8,000 increase to equity
It immediately has an $8,000 Accounts Payable liability, even with no loan agreement signed
It records an $8,000 decrease in liabilities
questions.explain: Buying on credit creates an Accounts Payable liability right away — a loan agreement is not required for a liability to exist.

questions.q: Which Oracle Fusion module exists specifically to manage the Accounts Payable liability?
options: Oracle Fusion Assets
Oracle Fusion Payables
Oracle Fusion Receivables
Oracle Fusion Cash Management
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Payables records supplier invoices, tracks what's owed and when, processes payments, and feeds the resulting liability into the General Ledger.
